title: UNM Hosts First Quantum Industry Day in New Mexico
html:
Insider Brief

  • The University of New Mexico’s Quantum New Mexico Institute (QNM-I) hosted its inaugural Quantum Industry Day on November 6, bringing together industry representatives, researchers, national laboratories, state leaders and investors.
  • The event featured discussions on New Mexico’s quantum ecosystem, research collaboration, company funding and commercialisation, alongside a tour of the Roadrunner Quantum Lab.
  • Companies including Atom Computing, Quantinuum, IonQ, QuEra Computing, Infleqtion and Diraq participated in presentations and discussions about the state’s quantum industry.

PRESS RELEASE — The University of New Mexico’s Quantum New Mexico Institute (QNM-I) brought together industry representatives, researchers, national laboratory partners, state leaders and investors for its inaugural Quantum Industry Day on Nov. 6. The all-day event concluded UNM’s 2026 Research and Discovery Week and highlighted New Mexico’s growing quantum capabilities, opportunities for collaboration and the companies helping expand the state’s quantum economy.

“Quantum Industry Day showed what happens when New Mexico’s research strengths, national laboratory expertise, industry partners, and state leaders come together around a shared goal,” said Barbara Rodriguez, UNM provost and executive vice president for Academic Affairs. “QNM-I is helping position New Mexico as a national leader in the quantum economy. UNM is proud to be part of building that future through discovery, education, and partnerships that create real opportunities for our students and our state.”

The morning program opened with welcoming remarks from Rodriguez, followed by presentations from:

  • Rob Black, Cabinet secretary, New Mexico Economic Development Department
  • Bob Ledoux, professor and director, QNM-I, UNM
  • Ivan Deutsch, distinguished professor and director, CQuIC, UNM
  • Jennifer Strabley, Vice president and general manager, Quantinuum
  • Carleton Coffrin, Quantum Science coordinator, Los Alamos National Laboratory
  • Jen Gaudioso, director of the Center for Computing Research, Sandia National Laboratories

The morning session concluded with a Quantum New Mexico panel that brought together representatives from QuEra Computing, Qunnect-NM, Mesa Quantum, IonQ and Elevate Quantum to discuss the state’s quantum ecosystem.

The afternoon program, hosted by Roadrunner Venture Studios, included a tour of the Roadrunner Quantum Lab led by David Kistin, the lab’s director. The program also featured a panel discussion on funding quantum companies in New Mexico. Nora Meyers Sackett, director of the Technology and Innovation Office, moderated the discussion with Max Gruner, director of Economic Development for the City of Albuquerque, and Quintin Rizek, manager of Investment Analysis at Roadrunner Venture Studios.

A company showcase featured presentations from:

  • Atom Computing
  • Bandelier Technologies
  • QPICs
  • Quantum Machines
  • SELA Photonics
  • Diraq
  • Classiq
  • Vescent Technologies
  • Monarch Quantum
  • Infleqtion

UNM President Goldstein closed the event with remarks at the reception, underscoring The University’s commitment to QNM-I and to the growth of quantum research, education and economic development in New Mexico.

“Our goal for Industry Day was to turn introductions into lasting collaborations,” said Bob Ledoux, QNM-I director. “The enthusiasm and willingness to work together were clear. Now we want to build on those connections through joint research, hands-on opportunities for students, and partnerships that help companies innovate and grow in New Mexico. That is QNM-I’s mission in action.”

Throughout the day, participants connected across research, industry, government, and investment communities, exploring opportunities to advance quantum research and commercialization in New Mexico. QNM-I thanks the speakers, organizers, and partners who made the event possible and looks forward to building on these connections at next year’s industry day.

Mohib Ur Rehman

MENTIONED IN THE ARTICLE

The University of New Mexico, located in Albuquerque, New Mexico, is a public research university. It was established in 1889 by the New Mexico Territorial Legislature. Being the state's second oldest university, it's one of the two flagship universities in New Mexico and boasts the highest enrollment, with more than 25,400 students in 2021.

Atom Computing builds quantum computers using nuclear spin qubits formed from arrays of optically-trapped neutral atoms.

Quantinuum builds full-stack quantum computing solutions for practical deployment. Leveraging proprietary enhancements to trapped-ion QCCD architecture, the company has launched multiple commercial hardware generations that deliver leading two-qubit gate fidelity and industry-topping accuracy.

IonQ is a developer in trapped ion quantum computing founded in 2015 that actively applies its technology to the aerospace and defense sectors. The company empowers satellite-based quantum networks and quantum enabled drones to improve positioning, navigation, and timing resilience in GPS denied environments, and collaborates with industry leaders like Airbus to optimize aircraft loading.

QuEra Computing uses research on neutral atoms, developed at Harvard University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, as the basis for a scalable, programmable quantum computer solution. QuEra’s quantum processing technology is based on trapping, energizing, and shuttling atoms with laser beams.

Infleqtion, founded in 2007 at the University of Colorado Boulder, specializes in neutral atom quantum technology for the aerospace and defense sectors. The company is heavily involved in orbital infrastructure, notably supplying atomic clocks and contributing quantum sensors to NASA's Cold Atom Lab and the Quantum Gravity Gradiometer Pathfinder mission to enhance space navigation, timing, and Earth observation capabilities.

Diraq is a full stack quantum company which is building a quantum computer using silicon CMOS-based spin qubits.

Classiq Technologies specializes in quantum computing software, focusing on enabling the design, optimization, analysis, and deployment of quantum algorithms. It develops a high-level quantum algorithm design platform (IDE, compiler, “OS”) that transforms functional models into optimized, hardware-aware quantum circuits to address the challenge of gate-level complexity. It emphasizes abstraction, circuit synthesis, and resource optimization, working with enterprises, researchers, and hardware/cloud providers to deliver scalable quantum software.

Monarch Quantum is a California-based company founded in 2025 that develops integrated photonics hardware and Quantum Light Engines™ for quantum technologies. The company supplies ruggedized, chip-scale laser systems to the aerospace and defense sectors, providing ultra-precise sensing for space-deployed gravity gradiometer instruments in collaboration with NASA and Infleqtion.
